subject: Clarify hosted-API data transfer notice & proposed privacy snippet
messages:
From: Karen Holt <karen.holt@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Yates <t.yates@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification: Data transfer and subprocessors in Redwood DPA

Kimberly —

Thanks for sharing the DPA draft during the procurement review. I read through Exhibit B and had a couple of quick items we need clarified before legal can sign off:

1) Data transfers: Exhibit B references "transfers to third countries" and mentions industry-standard safeguards. Can you confirm whether Redwood uses the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) / UK Addendum for transfers, and whether those will be attached to the signed DPA or performed via an account-level portal? We need explicit language for our procurement pack.

2) Subprocessors: The DPA has a paragraph that Redwood may engage subprocessors and will provide a list "upon request." Our vendor policy requires either: (a) a published current list with automated notice of additions at least 30 days in advance, or (b) an agreement that we may terminate or object. Can you confirm which option Redwood supports?

3) Log retention & hosted API: We noticed the hosted API product collects request/response logs for troubleshooting and tool improvement. Can you confirm retention windows, anonymization practices, and whether customers can opt out of non-essential logging while still using the hosted API?

I've attached a redline (acme_redline_dpa_v2.docx) with inline comments. Would appreciate a short written response for procurement; if easier, we can take a 30-minute call next Tue afternoon PT.

Thanks —
Karen Holt
Senior Counsel, Acme Analytics
Attachment: acme_redline_dpa_v2.docx (docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Karen Holt <karen.holt@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Data transfer and subprocessors in Redwood DPA

Karen —

Appreciate the clear redline and the procurement checklist. Quick answers below and a proposed public-facing snippet attached (proposed_privacy_snippet.txt) that we can use in the privacy page / DPA exhibit:

1) Transfers: Redwood acts as a processor for hosted API customers. For EU -> US transfers we offer two mechanisms depending on customer preference: (i) execution of the EU SCCs (we provide an executed annex/attachment to the DPA), or (ii) transfers based on an approved transfer mechanism where available (e.g., UK Addendum for UK customers). We will include the executed SCCs/UK Addendum as an exhibit to the customer DPA and make them accessible via the account portal upon signature.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a published, up-to-date subprocessors page and commit to notifying customers at least 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that will process customer content. We can also accept the typical procurement-friendly objection window: customers may notify us within 15 days of the notice to discuss reasonable concerns; if unresolved for certain high-risk scenarios, contract remedies are available.

3) Hosted API logs: Default hosted API logging retains request/response metadata and aggregated telemetry for 30 days; request/response content used for model improvements is retained for 90 days and then deleted unless the customer opts-in. We can accommodate an opt-out for use-of-data for product improvement and we offer dedicated plans with logging disabled or routed to customer-managed storage for an additional compliance fee.

Next steps:
- Attached is suggested public-facing phrasing for the privacy page and the DPA exhibit (proposed_privacy_snippet.txt).
- Laura and Aditya are looped to confirm the legal/ops wording and whether the 30/90-day windows are fine to present publicly.

If that works, let us know whether you'd like the final DPA with SCCs attached via DocuSign or delivered as a signed PDF. We're available for a quick call Tue 2/3 PM PT.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_privacy_snippet.txt (text)

Karen / Tom —

Thank you for the checklist and the constructive edits. We've reviewed internally (Legal + Product + Ops) and propose the following final public-facing language and contractual commitments for inclusion in the DPA exhibit and the privacy page: 

Proposed public-facing privacy & DPA exhibit language:
"Redwood Inference acts as a processor of customer-provided content for hosted API customers. We execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or an equivalent UK Addendum for transfers from the EEA/UK to the United States. Executed SCCs/UK Addenda will be appended as exhibits to the customer’s DPA and made accessible from the customer’s account portal upon signature.

Redwood maintains a publicly available list of subprocessors and will provide automated notice at least 30 days prior to the onboarding of any new subprocessor. Customers may raise objections within 15 days of such notice and we will work in good faith to address reasonable concerns.

Customers may request that Redwood not use Customer Content for model improvement; such requests will be implemented within five (5) business days from receipt. For customers requiring stricter control, Redwood offers dedicated deployment options and the ability to route logs to customer-managed storage. Details and pricing are available via the Redwood Console or your account representative."

Operational notes / timeline:
- We will update the public privacy page and DPA exhibit with the above language and a link to the subprocessors page by 2026-03-05.
- Executed SCCs/UK Addenda will be appended to the DPA and delivered via DocuSign; draft DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-Redwood-DPA-2026
- Ops will enable the opt-out flag in the account settings UI and confirm the 5-business-day implementation SLA for opt-outs.

Please confirm if the wording is acceptable; if so we will route the DPA for signature and update the privacy page.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
